title: Conditionals & Time Clauses
description: たら・ば・と・なら, 前に/後で/てから, ながら, 間に, とき, のに, ても, なければいけない, ないでください.

questions.prompt: {明日|あした}{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}っ（　）、{家|いえ}にいます。
questions.explanation: **た-form + ら** = 'if/when …'. Take the plain past and add ら: 降った → 降ったら.
notes: This mixes たら and ば. The ば-form of 降る is 降れば.
てら isn't a form. The conditional is built on the た-form: 降ったら.
と attaches to the dictionary form (降ると), not the た-form.
questions.translation: If it rains tomorrow, I'll stay home.

questions.prompt: このボタンを{押|お}す（　）、{水|みず}が{出|で}ます。
questions.explanation: **Dictionary form + と** = 'whenever/if A, B (automatically) happens'. It's used for natural consequences, machines and directions.
notes: で can't attach directly to a verb's dictionary form.
押すて isn't a form. The て-form of 押す is 押して.
押すに isn't a conditional. に after a dictionary form usually expresses purpose (with 行く) or appears in set phrases.
questions.translation: When you press this button, water comes out.

questions.explanation: The **ば-conditional** of an い-adjective: drop い and add **ければ**: 安い → 安ければ ('if it's cheap').
notes: と follows the full adjective (安いと), not 安けれ.
The て-form is 安くて, which can't follow 安けれ.
The たら form is 安かったら, which can't follow 安けれ.
questions.translation: If it's cheap, I'll buy it.

questions.prompt: A：{来週|らいしゅう}、{京都|きょうと}に{行|い}きます。　B：{京都|きょうと}に{行|い}く（　）、{金閣寺|きんかくじ}がおすすめですよ。
questions.explanation: **〜なら** = 'if (it's the case that) …'. It picks up a topic the other person mentioned and gives advice about it.
notes: まで ('until') doesn't fit a piece of advice.
ので ('because') makes B's sentence illogical: 'Because you go to Kyoto, Kinkakuji is recommended.'
のに ('even though') expresses surprise or frustration and doesn't make sense here.
questions.translation: A: I'm going to Kyoto next week. B: If you're going to Kyoto, I recommend Kinkakuji.

questions.prompt: {寝|ね}る（　）、{歯|は}を{磨|みが}きます。
questions.explanation: **Dictionary form + 前に** = 'before doing …'. The verb before 前に is always the dictionary form, even in past sentences.
notes: ながら attaches to the ます-stem (寝ながら).
たら attaches to the た-form (寝たら).
後で needs the た-form (寝た後で). 寝る後で is ungrammatical.
questions.translation: I brush my teeth before going to bed.

questions.prompt: {宿題|しゅくだい}をした（　）、ゲームをします。
notes: ながら attaches to the ます-stem (しながら).
までに ('by …') follows the dictionary form or a noun, and 'by having done homework, I play' makes no sense.
前に needs the dictionary form (する前に). It can't follow した.
questions.translation: I'll play games after doing my homework.

questions.prompt: {音楽|おんがく}を{聞|き}き（　）、{勉強|べんきょう}します。
questions.explanation: **ます-stem + ながら** = 'while doing …'. It describes two simultaneous actions by the same person, and the main action comes last.
notes: ても attaches to the て-form (聞いても), not the ます-stem 聞き.
から attaches to a full form (聞くから, 'because') or a て-form (聞いてから, 'after'), not the bare stem.
たら attaches to the た-form (聞いたら).
questions.translation: I study while listening to music.

questions.prompt: {手|て}を{洗|あら}って（　）、{食|た}べてください。
questions.explanation: **て-form + から** = 'after doing … / once you've done …'. It stresses the order of the two actions.
notes: まで doesn't follow a て-form.
ので follows a plain form (洗うので), not a て-form.
のに follows a plain form and means 'even though'.
questions.translation: Please wash your hands before you eat. (lit. after washing, eat)

questions.prompt: {赤|あか}ちゃんが{寝|ね}ている（　）に、{料理|りょうり}をします。
questions.explanation: **〜間に** = 'while/during (a period), do something (once)'. 間 without に means the action lasts the whole period.
notes: 上 means 'on/above'. It isn't a time expression here.
下 means 'under'.
中 doesn't follow 寝ている. It's used as 〜中 with nouns (仕事中).
questions.translation: I cook while the baby is sleeping.

questions.prompt: {子供|こども}の（　）、よく{川|かわ}で{泳|およ}ぎました。
questions.explanation: **Noun + の + とき** = 'when (I was) …'. With verbs and adjectives: 若いとき, 暇なとき, 行くとき.
notes: 子供のまえ would mean 'in front of the children'.
子供のあと isn't a natural time expression.
ながら attaches to verb stems, not to nouns with の.
questions.translation: When I was a child, I often swam in the river.

questions.prompt: {熱|ねつ}がある（　）、{学校|がっこう}に{行|い}きました。
questions.explanation: **〜のに** = 'even though …', often with a sense of surprise or frustration. Having a fever and still going to school is a contrast.
notes: なら ('if') doesn't fit a sentence about something that already happened.
まで means 'until'. 'Until I had a fever' doesn't fit here.
ので ('because') gives the reason. 'Because I had a fever, I went to school' is illogical.
questions.translation: Even though I had a fever, I went to school.

questions.prompt: {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}って（　）、サッカーの{試合|しあい}はあります。
questions.explanation: **て-form + も** = 'even if …'. The game takes place regardless of the rain.
notes: 〜ては is used in patterns like てはいけない ('must not'). It doesn't mean 'even if'.
The て-form already ends in て, so adding で is ungrammatical.
が can't follow the て-form.
questions.translation: Even if it rains, the soccer match will be held.

questions.prompt: {明日|あした}までにレポートを{出|だ}さ（　）いけません。
questions.explanation: **〜なければいけません** = 'must / have to …' (literally 'if you don't, it won't do').
notes: ないで + いけません isn't a pattern. ないで is used for 'without doing' or ないでください.
なくて + いけません isn't the obligation pattern. Use なければ or なくては.
なくてもいい means 'don't have to'. なくてもいけません is contradictory.
questions.translation: I have to hand in the report by tomorrow.

notes: なくてください isn't a form. Use ないでください.
Past なかった can't be used in a request.
なく is an adverbial form. It can't be followed by でください.

questions.prompt: {大学|だいがく}を{卒業|そつぎょう}する（　）、{日本|にほん}にいるつもりです。
questions.explanation: **まで** = 'until', for a state or action that continues up to a point (いる = keep being there). **までに** = 'by (a deadline)', for a one-time action.
notes: ので ('because') has the same problem.
から ('because/from') makes it 'because I graduate, I'll stay', which doesn't make sense.
までに is for a deadline for a single action (卒業するまでに論文を書く). いる is an ongoing state, so it needs まで.
questions.translation: I plan to stay in Japan until I graduate from university.

questions.prompt: もっと{勉強|べんきょう}すれ（　）よかったです。
questions.explanation: **ば-form + よかった** = 'I should have …' (regret). すれ is part of the ば-form of する: すれば.
notes: すれて isn't a form.
The たら form would be したらよかった, which can't follow すれ.
と attaches to the dictionary form (すると), not すれ.
